# Leaderboard of branch `agent/search` (generated by `python -m bmtbench.report` in the isolated worktree; protocol v1.1, amendments A1-A8)

This file is the agent branch's own report (`agent/LEADERBOARD.md`); it does not replace `bench/LEADERBOARD.md`. Every row is
tied to a content hash: learned models are named `<name>~<first 8 hex of sha256(config + fold checkpoints)>`, every prediction
file is registered by its sha256 in `agent/models.json`, and the generators refuse a file that does not match its row.

Data: Binance Vision spot archives (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, attribution: Binance Vision; not affiliated with or endorsed by Binance).
These tables are derived from that data and carry the same licence. Research evaluation only.

Rows: 393,407 hourly and 80,307 daily forecast origins, 62 assets with rows (47 trained-on, 15 never trained on), four unseen
calendar folds 2023-01 .. 2026-10. Every model is scored on the same rows. `sPL` = asset-equal scaled pinball over 21 quantiles
(lower is better). Intervals are 95 % block-bootstrap (weekly / 4-weekly calendar blocks, 1,000 resamples); skills against a
reference are paired.

Learned rows of this branch (`bmt-*` phase-2 rows are registered by prediction-file hash only):

{{ROWS}}

`bmt2-ohlc+cal` = promoted by the input search (bar range + Garman-Klass + calendar inputs); `bmt2-ohlc`, `bmt2-base` = the steps
before it; `+ic10` = with the ranking loss; `@t` = the 0.11M size; `-sym` = 2-pass flip-averaged; `bmt2-syn-*` = the same model
trained on synthetic bars only (permissive tier), `-ctx256` = 256-bar context.

## Reading it

- Promoted by the search (validation only), then scored once on the unseen folds: `bmt2-ohlc+cal`. Against the Timestral
  reference pipeline it gains 1.04 % [0.88, 1.21] / 0.75 % [0.59, 0.90] / 1.12 % [0.85, 1.38] sPL at hourly h 1 / 6 / 24 and
  0.65 % [0.40, 0.90] at daily h 1; against Timestral with a 2,048-bar context 0.91 % / 0.43 % / 0.36 %, all separated; against
  GARCH(1,1)-t 1.0-1.3 % everywhere including daily h 5; against the production Timestral kernel (fast) 1.7-1.9 % hourly.
  Daily h 5 against Timestral is not separated (+0.33 % [-0.09, 0.74]). The gain over the phase-2 model is 0.44 % [0.36, 0.52]
  at hourly h 1, shrinking to 0.16 % at h 24.
- The 0.11M model scores the same as the 0.82M one within 0.05 %.
- What the search did not find: nothing else passed for pinball. Volume, taker-buy share, long-memory volatility scalars,
  vol-of-vol, a second token stream of 256 daily bars, BTC / ETH returns, market breadth, peer baskets, BTC range, and realised
  variance from 5-minute returns (with its downside share) each moved validation sPL by less than 0.1 %.
- Ranking loss: promoted on validation (rank IC +0.018 at h 1), NOT confirmed on the unseen folds. At size s the test IC is
  0.068 / 0.060 / 0.043 (h 1 / 6 / 24) against 0.066 / 0.061 / 0.053 without it, at size t 0.067 / 0.065 / 0.052 against
  0.062 / 0.052 / 0.041; pinball is 0.35-0.5 % worse, and under the daily rotation rule it loses more than the model without it.
- Bot-usable tier: the same model trained on synthetic bars only gives up 0.3-0.6 % hourly (0.38 / 0.30 / 0.54) and 0.5-0.7 %
  daily against the research weights. It still beats the Timestral reference pipeline at every hourly horizon
  (0.66 % / 0.45 % / 0.58 %), GARCH everywhere, and the production Timestral kernel by 1.1-1.5 %; it ties Timestral on daily
  bars and is 0.2 % behind the 2,048-context Timestral at h 24. The 256-bar variant costs a further 0.1-0.2 %.
- Tradable value (section below): the medians carry real rank information (rank IC 0.05-0.07, two to three times Timestral's),
  worth 5 bp gross per hourly long-short trade and 14 bp at 24 h, against 8 bp of round-trip cost for the two legs at maker-tier
  fees and 40 bp at taker fees. Of the 240 net-of-cost intervals in the tables below exactly one is above zero: Timestral with
  the 2,048-bar context, 24 h long-short at maker-tier costs (+7.3 bp [0.5, 15.1]). The promoted model's own 24 h long-short net
  is +5.8 bp [-1.3, 12.6]. Threshold rule, daily rotation and volatility-timed sizing show nothing for anyone.
- Scale of the whole contest: the best model is 4.5 % better than a Gaussian random walk at hourly h 1.
- Caveats: Timestral's and Chronos-2's pretraining data are not disclosed (older folds may be in-sample for them); the phase-2
  recipe was chosen with F1 / F3 test numbers visible (A4); two folds of the promoted configs are refits (A6); the phase-2 placebo
  failed its original form at one horizon (A1); one exchange, spot only; costs in the tradable tables are assumptions.

## Tradable value on the unseen folds

Costs are assumptions, not measured fills: round trip 4 bp (maker-tier fees, no spread paid) or 20 bp (taker: 2 x 7.5 bp fee +
2 x 2.5 bp half-spread / slippage); no market impact, no funding; the long-short test assumes shorting is possible.
IC = mean cross-sectional Spearman correlation of forecast median and outcome per origin. L/S = long the top fifth by median,
short the bottom fifth, per origin, bp of one leg (net = gross - 2 x cost). Rule = long-only, buy when the median exceeds the
round-trip cost, net bp per trade (the random-walk alternative never trades).

Reading: no forecaster shows a robust edge after costs. One of 240 net intervals is above zero, fewer than chance alone would
give; the ranking-loss model makes the rotation worse, not better.

## Speed

One row = one 512-bar context -> 4 horizons x 21 quantiles for `bmt` / `bmt2` (24 steps x 21 for the reference pipelines, one
horizon for the `tsfm16` kernel). RTX 5090 shared with production servers (their load at the start of each run is in the last
column; numbers move +-30 % with it and are lower bounds), CPU = Xeon E5-2697 v4 (AVX2) on a host at load average about 80 of 72
threads. Host-device transfer and the pipe round trip are included. Mojo-vs-PyTorch parity on the self-test vectors: 2e-6 (CPU)
and 5e-6 to 4e-5 (GPU) scale units, tolerance 2e-4. Timestral rows are the measurements of the first stage, not re-run.

{{SPEED}}

The promoted size-t model forwards 218k rows/s on the GPU (14x `timestral-fast`, 39x `timestral-max`) and 24k rows/s on 12 CPU threads;
a single row takes 0.3 ms on one CPU thread.
